original_hypothesis: Important factual content that is absent from the initial HTML but becomes available only after client-side rendering or user interaction may create a machine/AI accessibility gap.
final_hypothesis: Relevant structured-data annotations that are available only after client-side rendering are unavailable to non-JavaScript machine readers from the initial HTML representation. While this does not completely hide factual information if the text is server-rendered, it creates a measurable semantic extraction gap that degrades programmatic confidence.

evidence: All text in the raw HTML payload.
Visually hidden FAQ answers are structurally present in raw HTML.
3 JSON-LD blocks (including FAQPage) in rendered DOM.
Non-JS reader successfully extracts text but must rely on NLP heuristics to structure FAQs.
JS-enabled reader extracts FAQs with 100% precision via the FAQPage schema.

cross_site_results: Sites exhibit diverse rendering paths: A (server-rendered JSON-LD), B (client-rendered), C (no JSON-LD).
Server-rendered JSON-LD is common and possible (e.g., Allbirds PDP).
counterexamples: Stripe: No JSON-LD in either state, yet perfectly discoverable by LLM.
Adobe: Client-rendered JSON-LD, but all facts already present in HTML (no information loss).
detection_algorithm: 1. Fetch raw HTTP. 2. Fetch via Playwright (JS). 3. Compare JSON-LD blocks. 4. Validate if structured facts are missing from raw HTML to determine severity.
false_positive_safeguards: Ignore if JSON-LD is entirely absent from both states.
Validate HTML text presence before flagging Information Loss.

severity_guidance.high: Information Loss: Facts present in rendered JSON-LD are completely missing from the raw HTML text.
severity_guidance.medium: Semantic Loss: Important schema (e.g., FAQPage) is render-only, but facts exist in raw HTML.
severity_guidance.low: Semantic Loss on non-critical metadata (e.g., WebSite, BreadcrumbList).

suggested_action: Modify SSR component to inject <script type='application/ld+json'> in the initial server payload.
generalization_assessment: The signal generalizes well. Sites clearly fall into categories of server-rendered vs client-rendered structured data.
